=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves, approximately 5 to 6, are clearly attached at the same node in a radial pattern, visible in all images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped tightly at the terminal end of the shoot)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf blade is undivided and attached directly to the stem)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (margins are smooth, though some leaves show minor physical damage/missing sections)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaves are longest in the middle and taper towards both the base and the apex)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (the tip comes to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (the base tapers down to a narrow angle where it meets the petiole)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a distinct central midrib with secondary veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible and distinct, arranged in a parallel fashion relative to each other as they extend towards the margin
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (the leaf surface reflects light, indicating a somewhat glossy texture)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (the surface appears smooth without visible hairs)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (the petioles are very brief, appearing to attach the leaves almost directly to the stem axis)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (the petioles appear round and slender in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the visible stem is thin and lacks the thickness or bark texture typical of a woody stem)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (the stem surface appears smooth)
    19. Stem color: green to reddish-green (the stem transitions from green to a reddish tint near the leaf attachment points)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no ridges or lenticels are visible on the stem)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): not observed (stipules are not clearly distinguishable in the images provided)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): not observed
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The leaves appear to be arranged in a terminal whorl. The venation is prominent and pinnate with a distinct midrib. Some leaves show minor physical damage with missing chunks from the margins.
